list: The official 55 trophies, as published by PlayStation and listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles on 2026-11-18
note: Names, descriptions and grades are the official list. Every guide below is written for this guide in our own words from the official description. The game released on 19 November 2026, so no guide step here has been verified in play yet: anything beyond the official description is labelled an estimate, and the exact spots and steps will be pinned down as players map them.

psnprofiles.label: PSNProfiles trophy list — grades and PSN progress counters

rockstar.label: Rockstar Games — Grand Theft Auto VI official page

usatoday.label: USA Today — GTA 6 launch live coverage, 19 Nov 2026

trophies.guide: The platinum is the last trophy you earn: it pops the moment the other 54 are done, so there is nothing to do for it directly. Follow the roadmap in order — story first, then the strangers' strands, then collectibles and activities — and keep the missables page open while you play, because the only trophies that can slip past you are the handful flagged there. This tracker counts all 54, so the platinum is simply the finish line.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
steps: Finish the story: chapters 1 to 4 and the final mission.
Clear the strangers' mission strands and the side activities.
Sweep the collectibles and the counted grinds, then check the tracker for stragglers.

trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this is the first trophy almost every player earns, minutes into the game. Play the opening as the game directs you — it teaches the basic movement, driving and switching between Lucia and Jason — and the trophy pops when the mission ends. Nothing here can be missed: it is the front door of the story.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
steps: Start a new game and follow the opening mission prompts.
Finish Gone Fishing; the trophy unlocks at the mission-complete screen.

trophies.guide: Chapter 1 is the first stretch of the story, built around Lucia's release from prison and her reunion with Jason in Leonida. Just play the story missions in order; side content can wait, since nothing in a chapter trophy asks for it. The trophy pops when the chapter's last mission ends. Story trophies cannot be missed — finish the chapter and it is yours.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost
steps: Play the story missions marked on the map until Chapter 1 closes.
Do not worry about collectibles yet; the roadmap saves them for stage 3.

trophies.guide: Chapter 2 continues Lucia and Jason's slide deeper into Leonida's criminal world after the opening job goes wrong. Keep following the story missions; the chapter trophy unlocks when its final mission is done. As with every chapter trophy, there is no missable step inside it — the only requirement is finishing the chapter.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
steps: Follow the story missions through Chapter 2.
The trophy pops at the end of the chapter's final mission.

trophies.guide: Chapter 3 brings the story into Vice City proper, the neon heart of Leonida. The missions here are longer and busier than the opening chapters, so expect more driving across the city and more shooting, but the trophy itself asks nothing extra: finish the chapter and it pops. If you are hunting efficiently, this is a good point to start noticing the activity spots the game introduces, without stopping the story for them.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
steps: Play the story missions through Chapter 3.
Note activity locations as you pass them; return for them in stage 4.

trophies.guide: Chapter 4 is the last full chapter before the finale, and the conspiracy Lucia and Jason are caught in comes to a head here. Finish its missions in order and the trophy unlocks. By the end of this chapter you should have most of the map open and most activities unlocked, which is why the roadmap puts the big collectible sweep after the story rather than during it.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
steps: Play the story missions through Chapter 4.
Once the chapter ends, the finale is next — keep a manual save before it.

trophies.guide: This gold trophy is the story's finish line: complete the final mission and it pops. The final mission is a single story beat, so it cannot be missed the way a side objective can — finish it and the trophy is yours. It is worth keeping a save from just before the finale (estimate: the game offers a pre-finale save point), in case the ending's choices matter for the choice-counted trophy, Actions Speak Louder.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
steps: Finish Chapter 4, then play the final mission to its end.
Keep a save from before the finale if you want to revisit its choices later.

trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a named story mission, and its trophy is one of the mission trophies that punctuate the campaign. Play the story until the mission appears on the map, then complete it; the trophy pops at the mission-complete screen. Mission trophies are unmissable in the sense that the mission itself is part of the story — you cannot finish the game without playing it.
trophies.name: Trust
steps: Advance the story until Breakfast Run is offered.
Complete the mission; no extra objective is needed for the trophy.

trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is a big set-piece story mission — a heist, the series' signature job — and its trophy unlocks when the mission is complete. Heists in this series usually have a planning stage and then the job itself; follow the mission's own objectives and the trophy follows. Like the other mission trophies, it is unmissable: the mission is on the critical path.
trophies.name: Break the Bank
steps: Advance the story until The Cartel Heist is offered.
Complete the heist's planning and execution objectives.

trophies.guide: Child's Play is a named story mission whose trophy pops on completion. The name suggests a job with a personal stake for Lucia or Jason, but the trophy itself asks only that you finish the mission — no special objective, no time limit, nothing to fail permanently. Play the story until it appears, then play it through.
trophies.name: Family Matters
steps: Advance the story until Child's Play is offered.
Complete the mission.

trophies.guide: Headliners is a named story mission, and DWNFALL is its completion trophy. The title hints at a mission that makes the news — a loud, public job — but the trophy is a plain mission-completion one: finish Headliners and it pops. It sits on the story path, so it cannot be missed.
trophies.name: DWNFALL
steps: Advance the story until Headliners is offered.
Complete the mission.

trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown is a story mission set around Vice City International Airport — the VCIA of the trophy's name. Complete the mission and the trophy pops. Note the airport location: it is also where the possibly-missable Catch Me If You Can trophy happens, so read that entry before you leave the airport area for the last time.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
steps: Advance the story until VCIA Takedown is offered.
Complete the mission, then check the Catch Me If You Can entry while you are still at the airport.

trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory is a named story mission — the military-sounding name suggests a large combat set piece — and Snow Storm is its completion trophy. It is one of the harder story missions by reputation of its name alone, so stock up on ammo and armour before starting (estimate: the game sells both at Ammu-Nation-style shops across Leonida). Finish the mission and the trophy pops; it is on the story path and cannot be missed.
trophies.name: Snow Storm
steps: Advance the story until Operation Savage Glory is offered.
Stock up before starting, then complete the mission.

trophies.guide: This gold trophy is the game's own 100% checklist, separate from the trophy list: story, strangers' strands, collectibles, activities and the counted grinds all feed into it, and PlayStation tracks it as a 0-to-100 counter. It is the last thing to chase — finish everything else first, then open the in-game stats and clear whatever categories are still short. Expect it to take the longest of any single trophy after the story.
trophies.name: A Long Road
steps: Finish the story and every strangers' strand.
Clear the collectibles, the activities and the counted grinds.
Open the in-game 100% checklist and mop up the categories still short.

trophies.guide: A stunt is a driving feat the game recognises — jumps, near misses, long air time and the like — and PlayStation counts them up to 250. This is a grind best done in the open world between missions, not chased in one sitting: fast cars, long straight roads and the jumps scattered around Leonida all feed it. Keep an eye on the PSN counter (0/250) and mix stunt driving into your normal travel so the number climbs on its own.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
steps: Drive fast and take jumps, ramps and near misses during normal play.
Use long highways and open ground to chain air time and near misses.
Check the PSN counter and finish the last few deliberately.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Leonida offers nine types of side activity, and this trophy asks for one taste of each — not mastery, just a try. The list itself is part of the game to discover (estimate: fishing, shooting range, drone racing, arcade games, bowling, meditation and racing are among them, from the other trophies' descriptions). Open the map and the activities menu as you explore, and tick each type off as you find it; the trophy pops on the ninth.
trophies.name: Master of None
steps: Open the activities list as you explore Leonida.
Try one of each of the nine activity types.
The trophy pops when the ninth type is tried.

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: There are 42 Shooting Range challenges, and this silver trophy demands a gold medal in every one — the hardest skill trophy on the list. Each challenge is a timed shooting drill; gold means fast, accurate shooting with the right weapon for the drill. Treat it as a late-game project: unlock the best weapons first, learn each drill's target pattern, and retry the stubborn ones one at a time rather than grinding them all in a row.
trophies.name: The Shootist
steps: Unlock the shooting ranges and try every challenge once.
Learn each drill's targets and the weapon it favours.
Return for golds one challenge at a time; leave the hardest for last.

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Top Fun runs drone races at 14 locations across Leonida, and this trophy wants a win at each one. Drone racing is its own skill — tight turns, gates and throttle control — so expect the first few wins to come slowly and the later ones faster as you learn the handling. Find each race on the map, win it, and move on; the PSN counter (0/14) shows which locations are still missing.
trophies.name: Top Fun
steps: Find a Top Fun drone race on the map and learn the drone's handling.
Win a race at each of the 14 locations.
Use the PSN counter to find the locations you have not won yet.

trophies.guide: Twenty different races, twenty wins — each race only counts once, so you cannot farm the same easy circuit twenty times. Leonida's races span cars, and probably bikes and boats too (estimate: the race types follow the series' usual mix), so variety is the point. Win the races you meet during the story and side content first, then sweep the remaining race markers on the map with the fastest vehicle you own.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
steps: Win races as you meet them in story and side content.
Sweep the remaining race markers with your fastest vehicle.
Each race counts once; the PSN counter shows 0/20.

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Cal is a fishing rival somewhere in Leonida — likely around the Leonida Keys or the Grassrivers wetlands, the state's fishing country (estimate from the setting Rockstar describes). Find his fishing challenge, out-fish him, and the trophy pops. Fishing in this series is a patience game: the right spot, the right lure and a steady hand on the line matter more than speed.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
steps: Find Cal's fishing challenge in Leonida's fishing country.
Beat his catch in the challenge.
If you lose, challenge him again — it is repeatable (estimate).

trophies.guide: Arcades are scattered around Vice City and Leonida, and this trophy asks you to finish one arcade game — see its credits roll or its end screen, not just play a round. Any arcade game counts, so pick the one you enjoy most and play it through. Arcades are also a good way to pass in-game time between missions.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
steps: Find an arcade in Vice City or elsewhere in Leonida.
Pick one game and play it to completion.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Andy is one of Leonida's strangers — side characters with their own mission strands, marked on the map as you explore. Play Andy's strand through to its final mission and this trophy pops. Stranger strands are separate from the main story, so they are easy to leave half-done; the roadmap puts them in stage 2, right after the story, so none of them is forgotten.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
steps: Find Andy's stranger marker on the map.
Play his missions in order to the final one.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Kenton is another of Leonida's strangers with a mission strand of his own. Follow his marker, play his missions in order, and the trophy pops at the strand's final mission. Stranger strands are self-contained stories, and each one ends with a trophy like this one — eight strands in total feed the Strangers & Freaks silver.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
steps: Find Kenton's stranger marker on the map.
Play his missions in order to the final one.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Billy is one of Leonida's strangers, and The Lone Rider is the trophy for finishing his strand. The name suggests a biker, so expect his missions to involve bikes and the open road. Find his marker, play the strand through, and the trophy pops at the final mission.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider
steps: Find Billy's stranger marker on the map.
Play his missions in order to the final one.

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Eight strangers across Leonida each have a mission strand, and this silver trophy wants all eight finished. The named stranger trophies — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone and Bret — are six of them, so two more strands exist beyond the named ones. Explore the whole state, follow every stranger marker you find, and finish each strand; the PSN counter (0/8) shows how many are done.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
steps: Finish the named strangers' strands: Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone and Bret.
Explore for the two remaining stranger markers.
Complete all 8 strands; the counter shows 0/8.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Randy is one of Leonida's strangers, and Supply & Demand is the trophy for finishing his strand. The name suggests a business of moving goods around the state, so expect driving and delivery missions. Find his marker, play the strand through to its final mission, and the trophy pops.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand
steps: Find Randy's stranger marker on the map.
Play his missions in order to the final one.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Tyrone is one of Leonida's strangers, and Spin On This! is the trophy for finishing his strand. The name hints at music — a DJ, a club, or the Vice City radio scene — so expect his missions to run through the city's nightlife. Find his marker, play the strand through, and the trophy pops at the final mission.
trophies.name: Spin On This!
steps: Find Tyrone's stranger marker on the map.
Play his missions in order to the final one.

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: There are 18 meditation spots across Leonida, and this trophy wants a session at each one. Meditation spots are quiet places — hilltops, beaches, the wilderness of Mount Kalaga National Park — so finding them is the real task; meditating itself is simple. Sweep the map region by region and use the PSN counter (0/18) to see how many spots remain.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
steps: Look for meditation spots in quiet places: beaches, hilltops, the national park.
Meditate at each spot you find.
Sweep region by region; the counter shows 0/18.

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bret is one of Leonida's strangers, and Fair Game is his strand's hunting trophy: track and hunt one unique animal for him. Leonida's wildlife runs from the Grassrivers wetlands to the Mount Kalaga wilderness (estimate from Rockstar's regions), so the hunt will take you into the wild parts of the map. Follow Bret's strand, find the animal's territory, and take the shot.
trophies.name: Fair Game
steps: Find Bret's stranger marker and start his strand.
Track the unique animal in its territory.
Hunt it and report back to Bret.

trophies.guide: Leonida hides collectible cards in sets, and this silver trophy wants three full sets completed. Cards are the classic open-world collectible: scattered across the map, in shops, alleys and landmarks. Collect them as you explore rather than in one dedicated sweep — you will pass most of them during the story and the stranger strands — then use the PSN counter (0/3) to see which sets are still short.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
steps: Pick up cards as you explore; they are scattered across Leonida.
Finish three complete sets.
The PSN counter shows 0/3 sets completed.

trophies.guide: WAiNK It is a Leonida-wide activity with 100 locations — the name suggests a photo or check-in style task at landmarks across the state. This is a pure exploration grind: visit the locations, do the WAiNK It action at each, and the silver pops at 100. Fold it into your exploration sweep for The Goodtime State, since both reward covering the whole map, and use the PSN counter (0/100) to track progress.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
steps: Find WAiNK It spots while exploring Leonida.
Do the WAiNK It action at each of the 100 locations.
Combine with the full-map exploration sweep.

trophies.guide: Leonida offers a set of open-world challenges — the game's own checklist of feats, separate from trophies — and this trophy wants 50 of them done. Challenges overlap heavily with the other trophies: stunts, races, collectibles and activities all count toward them, so most players will clear a large share without trying. Play broadly, check the challenges list in the game, and finish the last few deliberately.
trophies.name: One Last Thing
steps: Play broadly: stunts, races, collectibles and activities feed the challenges.
Open the in-game challenges list to see what is left.
Finish the last few deliberately; the counter shows 0/50.

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: This is a partner trophy: get to a 4-star wanted level while Lucia and Jason are together, then lose the cops and escape. Four stars means helicopters and heavy pursuit, so plan the escape before you cause the trouble — a fast car, a route out of the city toward the countryside or the water, and a hiding spot to wait out the search. Flagged as possibly missable: it needs your partner beside you, so do it during the story while partner missions are plentiful, not after the finale (estimate).
trophies.missable_note: Possibly missable: needs your partner with you, so do it while partner story missions are plentiful, before the finale.
trophies.name: Hot Together
steps: Play with your partner beside you during the story.
Raise a 4-star wanted level, then break line of sight and escape.
Lose the wanted level completely to pop the trophy.

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Another partner trophy: rob three shops in a row, back to back, with your partner, without ever losing your wanted level. The trick is speed and a clean getaway route between shops — pick three shops close together, keep the car running, and do not stop for a fight. Flagged as possibly missable for the same reason as Hot Together: it needs your partner with you, so do it during the story while partner missions are plentiful.
trophies.missable_note: Possibly missable: needs your partner with you; do it during the story, not after the finale.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy
steps: Pick three shops close together and plan a route between them.
Rob all three back to back with your partner.
Keep your wanted level the whole time; if it drops, start over.

trophies.guide: Leonida's streets, docks and airfields hold 100 vehicles to discover — drive one you have not driven before and it counts. This is a collector's trophy that rewards curiosity: try every car, bike, boat and aircraft you come across instead of sticking to one favourite. The PSN counter (0/100) shows progress, and the vehicle variety is widest in Vice City itself.
trophies.name: Whip It Good
steps: Drive every new vehicle you come across instead of one favourite.
Cover Vice City, the Keys, the docks and the airfields.
The counter shows 0/100 vehicles discovered.

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Combat Focus is GTA VI's slow-motion aiming mode, and this trophy wants five takedowns inside a single use of it. The setup matters more than the shooting: find a spot with five enemies grouped together, trigger Combat Focus, and work through them before the meter runs out. A busy shootout or a gang hideout is the place to try it; if the meter ends at four, just try again.
trophies.name: Gunslinger
steps: Find a fight with five or more enemies grouped together.
Trigger Combat Focus and take down five before it ends.
Retry in another shootout if the meter runs out early.

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: VCIA is Vice City International Airport, and an unscheduled departure means leaving by air without a ticket — stealing a plane and taking off. The airport is fenced and guarded, so get in with a fast vehicle, find a plane on the runway, and get airborne. Flagged as possibly missable: airport access may change after the story's airport mission, so try it while the VCIA Takedown mission is fresh (estimate).
trophies.missable_note: Possibly missable: airport access may change after the story's airport mission; try it around the VCIA Takedown mission.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
steps: Go to Vice City International Airport.
Find a plane on the runway and steal it.
Take off for an unscheduled departure.

trophies.guide: Rhinos are the series' tanks, and this trophy's joke — 'kinda hot in these Rhinos' — points at driving or fighting in one. The exact trigger is not spelled out by the official description, so treat this as an estimate: find a Rhino tank (likely at a military site or during a story mission), get in, and cause mayhem until the trophy pops. Flagged as possibly missable because tank access may be tied to one story moment.
trophies.missable_note: Possibly missable: the Rhino may only be reachable during one story moment; try it the first time you see one.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank
steps: Find a Rhino tank — a military site or a story mission is the likely place.
Get in and drive it; cause mayhem until the trophy pops.
If it does not pop, note the moment: tank access may be one-off.

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: This is the stealth robbery trophy: rob a jewelry store without being detected — no alarms, no witnesses raising the alarm, no police called. Plan it like a quiet job: go in when the store is empty or distracted, move fast, and get out before anyone notices. If the alarm trips, leave and try another store or another time; detection fails the attempt, not the trophy.
trophies.name: Sneakthief
steps: Pick a jewelry store and watch it for a quiet moment.
Rob it without tripping the alarm or being seen.
If detected, leave and try again at another store.

trophies.guide: Five bank vaults, five robberies, five escapes. Bank vaults are bigger jobs than shop robberies: plan the approach, bring your partner if the job allows it, and have the getaway ready before you go in. The PSN counter tracks vaults at 0/5, so you can see exactly how many are left. This is a silver because it asks for five clean escapes, not one lucky one.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
steps: Find a bank vault and plan the getaway before going in.
Rob the vault and escape; repeat for five vaults.
The counter shows 0/5 vaults robbed.

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Armored trucks drive set routes around Leonida carrying cash. Stop one — ram it, block it, or force the crew out — take the money and escape before the police close in. Trucks are a roaming target, so you can attempt this whenever you spot one; if the escape fails, another truck will come along.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
steps: Spot an armored truck on its route.
Stop it and take the cash.
Escape the police to pop the trophy.

trophies.guide: Leonida is a whole state — Vice City, the Leonida Keys, the Grassrivers wetlands, Mount Kalaga National Park, Port Gellhorn and Ambrosia — and PlayStation tracks exploration across 52 points of the map. This is the completionist's tour: drive, fly and sail into every corner until the map is filled in. Do it as a dedicated sweep after the story, and combine it with the WAiNK It locations and the meditation spots, which live in the same far corners.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State
steps: After the story, sweep the map region by region.
Cover the Keys, Grassrivers, Mount Kalaga, Port Gellhorn and Ambrosia.
The counter shows 0/52 exploration points.

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Nine gangs run illegal operations across Leonida, and this trophy wants one robbery from each gang's operation. Each gang holds different territory — the map's regions line up with gang turf — so this trophy is really a tour of Leonida's underworld. Find an operation, rob it, and move on to the next gang; the PSN counter (0/9) shows which gangs are still untouched.
trophies.name: Pest Control
steps: Find an illegal operation in a gang's territory and rob it.
Repeat for each of the nine gangs.
The counter shows 0/9 gangs robbed.

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Ocean Beach is Vice City's beachfront, and this trophy is a quiet moment: have a cocktail somewhere with a view of it. It is the game's breather trophy — no combat, no chase, just a drink with a view. Find a bar or a spot on Ocean Beach, order the cocktail, and enjoy the view; the trophy pops when the scene plays. Nothing about it suggests a one-off, so it can be done any time after Ocean Beach opens up.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…
steps: Go to Ocean Beach in Vice City.
Find a bar or viewpoint with a view of the beach.
Order the cocktail and let the scene play.

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: A vehicle showroom, a car, and a wall that is in the way: this trophy is a movie moment — drive a car straight out through the showroom's glass or wall 'in classic style'. Pick a showroom, pick a fast car, and aim for the exit that is not a door. It is a one-car stunt, repeatable if the first attempt stalls.
trophies.name: Capital Offense
steps: Find a vehicle showroom in Vice City.
Get a car inside or at its entrance.
Smash your way out through the glass or wall.

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Kolt & Associates run a bowling alley in Leonida, and this trophy is about the follow-through — the bowling motion itself, played properly. Go to the alley, start a game, and bowl with a proper follow-through until the trophy pops. Bowling is also one of the nine activity types for Master of None, so this visit does double duty.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
steps: Find the Kolt & Associates bowling alley.
Start a game and bowl with a full follow-through.
The trophy pops during the game.

trophies.guide: The description is the vaguest on the list — 'a partnership with mass appeal' — and PlayStation tracks it against a counter of 500, so the trigger is almost certainly a large counted total tied to the Lucia-and-Jason partnership (estimate: shared activities, or some repeated partner action, counted 500 times). Treat this as a long grind that fills in as you play together, and check the PSN counter (0/500) to see it climb. Flagged as possibly missable only because its trigger is unknown: if the 500 counts something that stops after the story, do partner activities while the story is running.
trophies.missable_note: Possibly missable: the trigger is a counted 500 total tied to the partnership, and it is not yet known what counts — do partner activities during the story, not only after it.
trophies.name: Personal Best
steps: Play partner activities with Lucia and Jason together.
Watch the PSN counter (0/500) to learn what counts.
Keep at it during the story; do not leave it all for after the finale.

trophies.guide: Choices made — for better or worse. This trophy is about the decisions Lucia and Jason make across the story: dialogue choices, approach choices, maybe the finale's ending choice. The description gives no number, so the trigger is likely a single significant choice, or the first choice you make (estimate). It is flagged as possibly missable because a choice, once made, may lock out its alternative — keep a save before big story decisions if you want to see both sides.
trophies.missable_note: Possibly missable: a story choice, once made, may lock out its alternative — keep a save before big decisions.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
steps: Play the story and make choices when the game offers them.
Keep a save before big story decisions.
The trophy pops on a significant choice (estimate).

trophies.guide: 'Second time's the charm' — this trophy is about retrying something and getting it right the second time. The official description does not say what, so the trigger is an estimate: fail an activity, a mission objective or a challenge, then succeed on the immediate retry. It is flagged as possibly missable only because it needs a failure first: if you play perfectly, you may never trigger it, so do not be afraid to fail an activity and try again.
trophies.missable_note: Possibly missable: it needs a failure followed by a success — a perfect playthrough may never trigger it.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
steps: Fail an activity or challenge, then succeed on the retry.
Any activity with a pass/fail result is a candidate.
The trophy pops on the successful second attempt (estimate).

trophies.guide: 'What the hell just happened?' — this is a trophy for a strange, surprising or scripted moment somewhere in Leonida, the kind of event that makes you stop and stare. The official description deliberately hides it, so the trigger is an estimate: a random event, a weird encounter, or a story beat that goes sideways. It is flagged as possibly missable because one-off moments are exactly the kind that pass by unnoticed — explore widely and pay attention to odd encounters.
trophies.missable_note: Possibly missable: a one-off strange moment — explore widely and do not rush past odd encounters.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
steps: Explore Leonida widely, including its odd corners.
Pay attention to strange encounters and random events.
The trophy pops when the moment happens (estimate).

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Ten Pin is bowling with a twist: bowl people over with a melee drive-by — attack from a moving vehicle with a melee weapon, bowling-pins style. The name is the guide: get a vehicle, get a melee weapon, and drive through a group of enemies swinging. It is a stunt trophy, not a bowling trophy, despite the name; the bowling alley trophy is the separate Let's Go Bowling.
trophies.name: Ten Pin
steps: Get a melee weapon and a vehicle.
Drive through a group of enemies swinging the weapon.
Knock them over drive-by style to pop the trophy.

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Marked Bills are dirty money, and your contacts launder them into clean cash — $250,000 of it, tracked by PlayStation. This is an economy trophy that fills in as you play: rob, earn marked bills, and launder them through your contacts whenever you can. It pairs naturally with the robbery trophies, so launder often instead of letting marked bills pile up.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
steps: Earn Marked Bills from robberies and jobs.
Launder them through your contacts.
Repeat until $250,000 is laundered; the counter tracks it.

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all of Leonida's shops — weapons, clothes, cars, food, anything that takes money. This is the spending half of the economy: the money you earn from jobs and robberies goes back out through the shops. Buy the weapons and upgrades you need anyway, and the counter (0/100,000) climbs on its own; if it is still short late in the game, spend the surplus on cars or clothes.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
steps: Buy weapons, upgrades, clothes and cars as you play.
Spend across many shops, not just one.
The counter shows 0/100,000 spent.

trophies.guide: There are eight garage properties to buy across Leonida, and this trophy wants all of them owned. Garages are both storage and investment: buy them as you earn money, and they give you somewhere to keep the 100 vehicles from Whip It Good. The PSN counter (0/8) shows how many you still need; the expensive ones are a late-game purchase.
trophies.name: Little Boxes
steps: Earn money from jobs, robberies and laundering.
Buy garage properties as they appear on the map.
Own all 8; the counter shows 0/8.

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Scooter Bros is Leonida's vehicle app, and this trophy wants ten vehicles registered to it. Register the vehicles you drive and own — scooters included, by the name — until the counter hits 10. It pairs with Whip It Good's 100 discovered vehicles, so register as you discover rather than saving it for the end.
trophies.name: On the Spot
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app and register a vehicle you own or drive.
Register ten vehicles in total.
The counter shows 0/10 registered.
